data.body:
CLOSE BLOCKED BY THE COMPLETION GATE, correctly, and file_impact is now widened.

The gate refused because commit 76c994fc97ba touches five files the recorded file_impact never
declared: _cli/_llm_commands.py, _config_resolvers.py, _errors.py, llm/errors.py and
llm/gate_admission.py. The work went beyond the reviewed plan.

Every one is defensible on its merits -- the new module, the two exception types, the error codes, the
config resolver, and the latent 'return 1' bug the implementation found. But defensible is not the
same as declared, and the gate is measuring the right thing: whether what shipped matches what was
reviewed.

THE MOST INTERESTING OMISSION IS gate_admission.py ITSELF -- the NEW MODULE at the centre of the
change. The reviewed plan described wrapping existing seams (plan_review/__init__.py,
completion.py, _mcp_llm.py) and named the test and the config paths, but never named the module that
would do the wrapping. That is easy to do and hard to notice: the plan reads complete because every
file it mentions is real, and the gap is a file that is absent rather than a claim that is wrong.

file_impact widened to all eleven paths with per-path reasons. _mcp_llm.py is retained even though it
ultimately needed NO edit -- making GateCongestedError an LLMError subclass with a retryable outcome
routed it through arms that already existed, which is a case of the design SHRINKING under review --
because dropping it silently would misrepresent the reviewed plan.

Widening file_impact is a material plan change, so the attestation is now stale-material and
review-plan must pass again before this can close. Re-running it. Not using --force: the gate is
correct that the shipped work exceeded the reviewed plan, and forcing past that would defeat exactly
the check that just did its job.
